findings.title: Migration raw SQL interpolation vulnerable to SQL injection and crashes on special characters
findings.body: The migration inserts site_settings values for embeddable_hosts via string interpolation into raw SQL (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`). If a host string contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, this will break the migration or allow SQL injection. Existing data from the deprecated `embeddable_hosts` site setting is untrusted/arbitrary and should be inserted using parameterized values (e.g. via ActiveRecord model creation or quoted values) instead of raw interpolation.

findings.title: category_id lookup query is fragile/broken
findings.body: The query `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` joins on an exact string match between category name and the embed_category setting value, which can easily fail to match (whitespace, case, slug vs name mismatches) and silently falls back to uncategorized without any error/log. This could silently assign the wrong category when migrating existing installations, losing user configuration state. No test covers this migration behavior.

findings.title: Host validation regex requires TLD of 2-5 chars, rejecting valid hosts like localhost or newer TLDs
findings.body: The regex `\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z` requires a dot and a 2-5 letter TLD. This rejects valid use cases such as `localhost`, single-label hostnames, or longer TLDs (e.g. `.technology`, `.photography`), which is a regression from the previous embeddable_hosts setting which did not enforce a strict host validation. This could block valid admin configurations without clear explanation (dev/testing with localhost is explicitly supported elsewhere in embed_controller.rb).

findings.title: update/destroy do not handle missing records
findings.body: In `update` and `destroy`, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil if the id doesn't exist (e.g., already deleted by another admin). `save_host(nil)` would raise a NoMethodError on `host.host =`, and `destroy` would raise NoMethodError on `host.destroy`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of a clean 404/error response.

findings.title: basePath type.replace only replaces first underscore occurrence
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` (without a global regex flag) only replaces the first underscore in the type string. If a model type name contains multiple underscores, matching against ADMIN_MODELS (which uses hyphens) will fail for all but the first underscore, potentially misrouting those types to the non-admin basePath.

findings.title: No negative/missing-host test for TopicEmbed category assignment
findings.body: The import spec only verifies that the post's category equals the embeddable_host's category when a matching host exists. There's no test verifying behavior when `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns nil (e.g., falls back to default/uncategorized category), which is a meaningful behavior change introduced by this PR (previously used SiteSetting.embed_category directly).
